# Summary

Adds **W8A8 MXFP8** quantization (8-bit weights + 8-bit activations, block_size = 32) for Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 **MoE** (FusedMoE) LLM models on Ascend NPU, continuing the NPU quantization work tracked in #21584. Both **online** (`--quantization mxfp8`) and **offline** (msmodelslim, flagless — selected by the checkpoint's `quant_model_description.json`) paths are supported and share the same fused-experts kernel. Requires Ascend A5 (Ascend 950) — the fused MoE MX kernels (`npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2`, `npu_dynamic_mx_quant`) are A5-only.

> #23795 (dense W4A4) has landed and this branch is merged up to `main`, so the diff is now the MoE MXFP8 delta only. It reuses the merged dense MXFP8 infrastructure — `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod`, the `Fp8Config` NPU dispatch, and `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme` (from #22352).

**Online quantization (`--quantization mxfp8`)**

- On the **Ascend NPU** backend, `Fp8Config.get_quant_method()` dispatches FusedMoE layers to the new `NPUMXFP8OnlineMoEMethod` (the `isinstance(layer, FusedMoE)` branch, mirroring the existing dense `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod` linear branch). It subclasses `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` and overrides only `create_moe_runner`, to attach the MXFP8 per-gmm kernels — weight creation, weight post-processing and the forward pass are the unquantized Ascend ones. On GPU the `FusedMoE` branch is untouched.
- BF16/FP16 expert weights `w13`/`w2` are quantised once at load via `npu_dynamic_mx_quant(dst_type = torch_npu.float8_e4m3fn)` — a 3D `[E, N, K]` input is accepted directly (no per-expert loop) — into `float8_e4m3fn` weights + UE8M0 (`float8_e8m0fnu`) block scales, kept as **non-contiguous transpose views**.
- Forward: on the `ascend_tp` dispatcher, `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` with **`quant_mode=3`** (count `group_list`) — the per-token MXFP8 activation quant is fused directly into routing, so the same kernel launch emits the sorted `float8_e4m3fn` payload *and* its `float8_e8m0fnu` block scale, saving a separate `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` pass — → **gmm1** `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2` (gate_up + swiglu + requant fused, **cumulative** `group_list`) → **gmm2** `npu_grouped_matmul` (**count** `group_list` + explicit `group_list_type`). The UE8M0 scale dtypes are passed explicitly; the e4m3 `x`/`weight` dtypes are left implicit. DeepEP has no MXFP8 dispatch dtype, so on that path the dispatcher keeps sending BF16 and gmm1 quantizes the hidden states itself via `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` before the fused kernel — both dispatchers reach gmm1 with the same input. Only the `ascend_tp` path is validated end-to-end on A5.
- **Fused-routing quant optimization:** the fused `quant_mode=3` scale comes back flat (`[N, K/32]`) instead of the pair-split `[N, K/64, 2]` layout gmm1 expects, so `_normalize_mxfp_scale` reshapes it before use. Verified via a standalone probe script (`npu_moe_init_routing_v2(quant_mode=3)` vs. the two-step `quant_mode=-1` + `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` reference) to be byte-identical (cos = 1.0) on Ascend A5 + torch_npu 2.10.0.post2, then confirmed end-to-end on the online and offline launch scripts — so this fused path is the only routing-quant implementation kept (no runtime toggle, no two-step fallback branch).

**Offline quantization (msmodelslim pre-quantized weights, flagless)**

- `W8A8_MXFP8` MoE checkpoints are detected from `quant_model_description.json` and handled by the new `ModelSlimMXFP8MoEScheme`, which registers `float8_e4m3fn` expert weights + `uint8` (E8M0, exponent + 127) block scales and delegates weight post-processing + forward to the **same** `NPUMXFP8MoEMethod` kernel (offline branch: reshape `[E, N, K/32] → [E, N, K/64, 2]` + transpose, no re-quant).
- **Router gate:** msmodelslim also quantises `mlp.gate` (`W8A8_MXFP8`). The gate is a `ReplicatedLinear`, so its quantization is now **description-driven** — for the offline `modelslim` path the gate receives the quant config and is dequantised correctly via `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme`; the online path keeps it in BF16 (unchanged). Previously the fp8 gate was cast to BF16 **without** its block scale, scrambling the router and producing garbage output; this is the fix that makes the offline path usable.

# Benchmark Results

Validated end-to-end on Ascend A5 hardware (Qwen3-30B-A3B). Both W8A8 MXFP8 modes (online and offline msmodelslim) are compared against the BF16 baseline.

## Performance

Both paths ship the FRACTAL_NZ expert-weight layout (review item 8). Against BF16, online and offline W8A8 MXFP8 deliver **~+44% throughput** and **~-30% TPOT / E2E latency**; the two modes are within noise of each other.

| Metric | BF16 (avg) | Online W8A8 (avg) | vs BF16 | Offline W8A8 (avg) | vs BF16 |
|--------|-----------|-------------------|---------|--------------------|---------|
| **Request Throughput (req/s)** | 3.03 | 4.37 | **↑ +44.2%** | 4.35 | **↑ +43.6%** |
| **Input Token Throughput (tok/s)** | 1191.70 | 1719.21 | **↑ +44.3%** | 1709.32 | **↑ +43.4%** |
| **Output Token Throughput (tok/s)** | 640.99 | 924.73 | **↑ +44.3%** | 919.41 | **↑ +43.4%** |
| **Total Token Throughput (tok/s)** | 1832.69 | 2643.95 | **↑ +44.3%** | 2628.72 | **↑ +43.4%** |
| **Mean E2E Latency (ms)** | 10101.74 | 7004.54 | **↓ -30.7%** | 7043.46 | **↓ -30.3%** |
| **Median E2E Latency (ms)** | 7159.17 | 4950.51 | **↓ -30.9%** | 4986.98 | **↓ -30.3%** |
| **P99 E2E Latency (ms)** | 38648.60 | 26909.35 | **↓ -30.4%** | 27005.87 | **↓ -30.1%** |
| **Mean TTFT (ms)** | 168.29 | 134.96 | **↓ -19.8%** | 136.54 | **↓ -18.9%** |
| **Median TTFT (ms)** | 153.14 | 133.13 | **↓ -13.1%** | 136.12 | **↓ -11.1%** |
| **P99 TTFT (ms)** | 1204.71\* | 231.07 | **↓ -80.8%** | 227.01 | **↓ -81.2%** |
| **Mean TPOT (ms)** | 47.44 | 32.79 | **↓ -30.9%** | 32.96 | **↓ -30.5%** |
| **Median TPOT (ms)** | 46.91 | 33.20 | **↓ -29.2%** | 33.24 | **↓ -29.1%** |
| **P99 TPOT (ms)** | 80.22 | 49.60 | **↓ -38.2%** | 49.81 | **↓ -37.9%** |
| **Mean ITL (ms)** | 47.44 | 32.81 | **↓ -30.8%** | 32.98 | **↓ -30.5%** |

> Improvement = `(quantized - bf16)/bf16` for throughput and `(bf16 - quantized)/bf16` for latency; positive values are a performance gain.
>
> \* The BF16 P99 TTFT is skewed by a single outlier run (3100.86 ms); the other two BF16 runs were 263.73 and 249.55 ms. Every quantized configuration is consistently low and stable here.

### FRACTAL_NZ weight layout (review item 8)

ND vs NZ on the same benchmark, everything else equal:

| Metric | Online: ND → NZ | Offline: ND → NZ |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Total Token Throughput (tok/s)** | 2592.53 → 2643.95 (**+2.0%**) | 2552.76 → 2628.72 (**+3.0%**) |
| **Mean E2E Latency (ms)** | 7146.17 → 7004.54 (**-2.0%**) | 7259.02 → 7043.46 (**-3.0%**) |
| **Mean TTFT (ms)** | 144.32 → 134.96 (**-6.5%**) | 145.93 → 136.54 (**-6.4%**) |
| **P99 TPOT (ms)** | 51.58 → 49.60 (**-3.8%**) | 52.73 → 49.81 (**-5.5%**) |

Not the ~10% the int paths saw, but consistent across both modes, so NZ is what this PR
ships. A standalone kernel probe on the same box (gmm1 + gmm2 only, 128 experts) measured
+1.4% on decode-shaped and +3.8% on prefill-shaped inputs against a 0.2-0.3% noise floor,
matching the end-to-end delta.

Two things worth recording, since neither is obvious from the int8 precedent:

- **The cast must precede the transpose.** `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2` asserts
  that weight and weight_scale carry the same transpose flag (`CheckMXTranspose`), and
  `npu_format_cast` returns a physically retiled, non-transposed tensor — so casting the
  already-transposed view fails outright with `transpositions are true/false`. The int8 MoE
  methods transpose first, but they carry no MX scale to keep in sync; the dense W4A8 path
  already uses the order adopted here.
- **Contiguous weights are not the answer.** Making weight and scale both contiguous is
  numerically correct but measurably slower (-6.2% decode at 128 experts), so the
  transpose views stay. A small-expert-count microbenchmark inverts this conclusion
  entirely (E=4 rates contiguous 58% *faster*), which is why the numbers above come from
  the real 128-expert shape.

## Accuracy (GSM8K)

Validated on Ascend A5 hardware (Qwen3-30B-A3B), three runs each. Both W8A8 MXFP8 modes stay within run-to-run noise of the BF16 baseline.

| Run | BF16 | Online W8A8 | Offline W8A8 |
|-----|------|-------------|--------------|
| Run 1 | 95.68 | 95.53 | 95.68 |
| Run 2 | 95.91 | 95.98 | 95.91 |
| Run 3 | 96.13 | 96.29 | 95.75 |
| **Average** | **95.91** | **95.93** | **95.78** |
| **vs BF16** | — | **↑ +0.03** | **↓ -0.13** |

> GSM8K accuracy (%); `vs BF16` is the average-over-average delta in percentage points.
> Both deltas are smaller than the 0.45 pp spread of the BF16 baseline's own three runs.

# Style / consistency with the merged NPU quant PRs (#22352, #23650, #23795)

- All NPU ops go through `torch.ops.npu.*`; **no top-level `import torch_npu`**, no `current_platform` guards (module stays importable on CUDA/CPU/AMD/XPU CI).
- **Online** returns the method directly from `Fp8Config.get_quant_method` (mirrors dense `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod`). **Offline** subclasses `ModelSlimMoEScheme` and delegates weight post-processing / forward to a `self.kernel` (`NPUMXFP8MoEMethod`), registered in `get_moe_scheme`'s `moe_quant_schemes` list — the same pattern as the int8 / W4A4 / W4A8 MoE schemes.
- MoE weight + scale are kept as **non-contiguous transpose views** (`.transpose(1, 2)` with no `.contiguous()`), with the expert weight cast to **FRACTAL_NZ before** that transpose; gmm1 uses the fused `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2`; the `group_list` count↔cumulative conversion is explicit (gmm1 cumulative, gmm2 count).

# Files Changed

**New**

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/schemes/modelslim_mxfp8_moe.py` | offline `ModelSlimMXFP8MoEScheme` for `W8A8_MXFP8` MoE checkpoints |

**Modified**

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py` | add the per-gmm kernel `NPUMXFP8MoEMethod` (online + offline `process_weights_after_loading`, `apply_fused_gmm1_swiglu` for w13, `apply` for w2); cast the expert weights to FRACTAL_NZ ahead of the transpose |
| `srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py` | `_is_nz_aligned`: add the fp8 branch — e4m3 is single-byte, so it shares int8's column rule. It previously fell through to the catch-all `True`, which no caller exercised (the packed-FP4 callers return early via `customize_dtype`, and dense MXFP8 never format-casts) |
| `srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/online_moe_methods.py` (new) | `NPUMXFP8OnlineMoEMethod(UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod)`, the `--quantization mxfp8` entry point |
| `srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/matmul.py` | add `GroupedMatmulSwigluQuant`, the reusable wrapper around `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2` |
| `srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/hidden_states_quant.py` → `quant.py` | rename + teach `HiddenStatesDynamicQuant` the `float8_e4m3fn` (`npu_dynamic_mx_quant`) dtype |
| `srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` | drop the hardcoded `dispatcher_output_dtype: "bf16"` that clobbered the value the NPU kernel had just set (it duplicated `NPUUnquantMoEMethod`) |
| `srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py` | stop rejecting DeepEP at runner construction |
| `srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py` | dispatch FusedMoE layers to `NPUMXFP8OnlineMoEMethod` under `is_npu() and use_mxfp8` |
| `srt/arg_groups/overrides.py` | skip the `mxfp8` → `flashinfer_trtllm` runner-backend override on NPU, so the backend stays `auto` and resolves to Ascend (it also gates FusedMoE's w1/w3 shard swap) |
| `srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py` | add `("W8A8_MXFP8", ModelSlimMXFP8MoEScheme)` to `get_moe_scheme`'s `moe_quant_schemes` |
| `srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/schemes/__init__.py` | export `ModelSlimMXFP8MoEScheme` |
| `srt/models/qwen3_moe.py` | make the router `gate` quant **description-driven** (offline modelslim only) so a quantised `mlp.gate` loads/dequantises correctly instead of being cast to BF16 without its scale |
| `docs_new/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx`, `docs_new/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/ascend_npu_quantization.mdx` | document MXFP8 MoE (Ascend support row + online/offline prose + router-gate note) |

# Status

**WIP / Draft.** Online (`--quantization mxfp8`) and offline (msmodelslim) MoE MXFP8 are both **validated end-to-end on Ascend A5** (see Performance above). GSM8K accuracy is within run-to-run noise of the BF16 baseline (see Accuracy above).

@OrangeRedeng's review is addressed. It was first applied as a single refactor commit (`6bd7056`), which garbled generation on A5 in a way that could not be bisected, so that commit was dropped and the review was redone one item at a time, each verified on A5 before the next:

| # | Item | Commit |
| - | ---- | ------ |
| 6 | offline checkpoints load flagless, drop `--quantization` from the docs | `9efe9998d` |
| 7 | rename `hidden_states_quant.py` → `quant.py`, teach it mxfp8 | `efe50dfa3` |
| 2, 5 | `GroupedMatmulSwigluQuant` wrapper + pick the matmul by `weight_prefix` | `2d06d61a5` |
| 1 | stop rejecting DeepEP; gmm1 quantizes when the dispatcher sends bf16 | `1efd2ca35` |
| 3, 4 | inherit `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, rename to `NPUMXFP8OnlineMoEMethod` | `ea24f248d` |
| 8 | `npu_format_cast` (NZ) | `d419aa41f` |

Re-validating the baseline first also surfaced three regressions from the preceding `main` merge, in which upstream restructured the NPU MoE layer (`fused_moe_method_npu.py` deleted, `moe_methods.py` / `moe_runner/ascend.py` / `npu/moe/*.py` added) and this PR's implementation was re-ported onto the new layout. None are review-related:

| Commit | Regression |
| ------ | ---------- |
| `e9b36bb5d` | the e8m0 block-scale dtype was resolved off `torch` instead of `torch_npu`; the grouped matmuls reject torch's dtype object, so every gmm1 died |
| `9ac21f5ff` | `--quantization mxfp8` forced `moe_runner_backend` to `flashinfer_trtllm` unconditionally, including on NPU. Beyond picking a runner that does not exist there, that flag also drives FusedMoE's w1/w3 shard swap and a 128-alignment round-up — and once item 3 above makes this method inherit `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, it matches the shard-swap list, loading every expert with gate and up exchanged. Silent degenerate output; this is what garbled the big-bang refactor |
| `969087364` | `ModelSlimMoEMethod.apply` reads `{w13,w2}_weight_offset` unconditionally; MXFP8 is a pure scale format with no zero point, so the offline scheme never created one |

# Related Issues

Part of #21584 (MXFP8/MXFP4 support on Ascend NPU for Qwen3 LLM). Builds on merged #23795 (dense W4A4) and #22352 (dense W8A8 MXFP8 — provides the dense linear MXFP8 method + `Fp8Config` NPU dispatch + `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme` this MoE work reuses).

+

+    quantised at load time) and the offline ModelSlim ``W8A8_MXFP8`` scheme

+    apart by weight dtype.

+    the dispatcher's ``npu_moe_init_routing_v2(quant_mode=3)`` emits the e4m3
+    payload and e8m0 scale as part of routing, and gmm1 re-quantises its own
+    output. Consequently gmm1 is a single fused kernel rather than a matmul plus
+    a separate activation, so the runner calls ``apply_fused_gmm1_swiglu`` for
+    w13 and ``apply`` only for w2.
+    """

+        super().__init__(quant_config=None)
+        self.matmul = GroupedMatmul()

+    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Quantise BF16/FP16 expert weights ``[E, N, K]`` to MXFP8 at load time.
+
+        Returns the e4m3 payload ``[E, N, K]`` and its e8m0 block scale
+        ``[E, N, K//64, 2]`` (block_size=32, already pair-split by the op).
+        """
+        if weight.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            logger.warning(
+                "NPUMXFP8MoEMethod: %s_weight dtype %s is not float16/bfloat16; "
+                "casting to bfloat16 before MXFP8 quantisation.",
+                weight_prefix,
+                weight.dtype,
+            )
+            weight = weight.to(torch.bfloat16)
+        # cpu offload may have moved the weight back to host memory.
+        if not weight.is_npu:
+            weight = weight.to(f"npu:{torch.npu.current_device()}")

+        self, layer: torch.nn.Module, weight_prefix: str
+    ) -> None:

+        # .contiguous(). The reduction loop scans the K-dim per output column,
+        # which the [E, N, K] row-major source gives at stride 1 through the
+        # transpose view (matches NPUMXFP8LinearMethod, msmodelslim's offline
+        # layout and vllm-ascend's AscendW8A8MXFP8DynamicFusedMoEMethod).
+        # .contiguous() would physically reorder to [E, K, N] row-major, making
+        # the inner-loop stride = N and tanking HBM bandwidth.
+        setattr(
+            layer,
+            f"{weight_prefix}_weight",
+            Parameter(weight.transpose(1, 2), requires_grad=False),
+        )
+        setattr(
+            layer,
+            f"{weight_prefix}_weight_scale",
+            Parameter(scale.transpose(1, 2), requires_grad=False),
+        )
+
+        if weight_prefix == "w13":
+            self._set_dispatcher_output_dtype(layer, "mxfp8")
+
+    def apply_fused_gmm1_swiglu(
+        self,
+        quant_info: "AscendQuantInfo",
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        expert_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+        pertoken_scale: torch.Tensor,
+        group_list_type,
+    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Gate/up projection, swiglu and requantisation in one kernel (gmm1).
+
+        Returns the e4m3 activations and their e8m0 block scale, i.e. exactly
+        what the w2 gmm needs, which is why the runner skips its activation step
+        for MXFP8.
+        """
+        e8m0_dtype = _require_e8m0_dtype()
+        # gmm1 wants a cumulative group_list while gmm2 keeps the COUNT form the
+        # dispatcher produces (group_list_type=1). The asymmetry is intentional.
+        group_list = expert_tokens.cumsum(0) if group_list_type == 1 else expert_tokens
+        return torch.ops.npu.npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2(
+            x=hidden_states,
+            weight=[quant_info.w13_weight],
+            group_list=group_list,
+            weight_scale=[quant_info.w13_weight_scale],
+            x_scale=pertoken_scale,
+            dequant_mode=2,
+            quant_mode=2,
+            dequant_dtype=torch.float32,
+            quant_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+            # e4m3 is implicit for these two — it is not in the op's QUANT_DTYPES.
+            x_dtype=None,
+            weight_dtype=None,
+            weight_scale_dtype=e8m0_dtype,
+            x_scale_dtype=e8m0_dtype,
+        )
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        quant_info: "AscendQuantInfo",
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        expert_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+        pertoken_scale: torch.Tensor,
+        output_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        weight_prefix: str,
+        group_list_type,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if weight_prefix != "w2":
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"NPUMXFP8MoEMethod.apply only serves the w2 gmm, got "
+                f"'{weight_prefix}'. gmm1 fuses swiglu into a single op and must "
+                f"go through apply_fused_gmm1_swiglu, which returns a scale too."
+            )
+
+        e8m0_dtype = _require_e8m0_dtype()
+        scale_args: Dict[str, Any] = {
+            "scale": [getattr(quant_info, f"{weight_prefix}_weight_scale", None)],
+            "per_token_scale": [pertoken_scale],
+            "scale_dtype": e8m0_dtype,
+            "per_token_scale_dtype": e8m0_dtype,
+            "x_dtype": None,
+            "weight_dtype": None,
+        }
+        return self.matmul.forward(
+            quant_info,
+            weight_prefix,
+            hidden_states,
+            expert_tokens,
+            output_dtype,
+            group_list_type=group_list_type,
+            transposed=True,
+            **scale_args,
+        )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#  NPUMXFP8FusedMoEMethod
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+class NPUMXFP8FusedMoEMethod(FusedMoEMethodBase):
+    """Online MXFP8 FusedMoE entry point (``--quantization mxfp8`` on A5).
+
+    Owns the BF16 weight placeholders and the runner wiring; the per-gmm work
+    lives in ``NPUMXFP8MoEMethod``, which quantises the weights to MXFP8 at load
+    time. The offline ModelSlim path reuses that same kernel via
+    ``ModelSlimMXFP8MoEScheme`` instead of this class.
+
+    TP only: MoE EP / DeepEP is not supported on this path.

## CI investigation

The current CI failures are **not caused by this PR's MXFP8 MoE changes**.

### 1. Non-CUDA platforms fail in an upstream DWDP import path

The MLX, Xeon, and Ascend/NPU jobs all fail while importing `ModelRunner`:

```
ModelRunner -> DwdpManager -> dwdp/vmm.py:11
from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cuda'
```

This unconditional CUDA-only import was introduced by upstream DWDP PR #29778 (commit `37a830b66`). It is outside this PR's diff from base `c0ed009f5` to head `e22b7bef8`; this PR does not modify `model_runner.py` or any `layers/moe/dwdp/` file.

The failed NPU case is `Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` HiCache, so it does not exercise the Qwen3/Qwen3.5 MoE MXFP8 code added here.

### 2. The Base GPU root failure is runner state, then fast-fail cascades

The first Base CI root-cause job (`base-c-test-8-gpu-h200 (0)`) runs a MiMo test, then its following DeepSeek MTP test aborts because every GPU still holds about 99 GiB from the previous server processes:

```
RuntimeError: GPU(s) still not idle after waiting 30s before setUpClass
```

The remaining H100/B200/DeepEP Base failures are the workflow's fast-fail cascade from that root job, rather than independent test or quantization failures.

No failing log contains an MXFP8 kernel/quantization assertion or a failure in the files changed by this PR. Lint and XPU checks passed.

**Conclusion:** this PR is blocked by the upstream DWDP non-CUDA import regression plus an independent dirty-GPU-runner failure. The DWDP import needs an upstream platform guard/lazy import; after that, the GPU job should be rerun on a clean runner.
